title: Apps made with AI builder Lovable exposed passport details and 200,000+ private messages
summary: Security researchers report that apps created with Lovable — a popular tool that lets you build a working app by describing it in plain words — left users' passport details and more than 200,000 private messages open to anyone who knew where to look.

title: AI uses more energy when you write in languages other than English
summary: University of Michigan researchers report that generative AI consumes more energy to handle non-English text than English.

title: LinkedIn and Monster remove 1,000+ fake job postings
summary: After an investigation by Canadian broadcaster CBC, LinkedIn and Monster took down more than 1,000 fake job ads.

title: Digital-rights group asks court to require warrants for license-plate camera searches
summary: The Electronic Frontier Foundation is asking a US appeals court to rule that police need a warrant before searching data from automated license plate readers — cameras that log where cars go.

title: The US flight halt came down to one router in Arkansas
summary: Previously covered on 2026-11-14: the FAA stopped departing flights nationwide for about 4.

title: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs 90 days after reporting them
summary: Google's Project Zero, its team that hunts security flaws in other companies' software, says it will make vulnerabilities public 90 days after reporting them to the vendor.

title: DeepSeek V3 rebuilt in about 200 lines of code
summary: A developer has published a compact version of DeepSeek V3, a large open AI model, written in roughly 200 lines of pure JAX — Google's library for numerical computing.

title: Old Bitly links are being hijacked
summary: A report says old Bitly short links — including one in a past Burger King tweet — are being taken over so they now point to different, unintended destinations.

title: Qwen4-Max is out
summary: The Qwen team has published Qwen4-Max, the newest flagship model in its Qwen AI family.

title: A Microsoft 365 outage is linked to chlorine gas exposure at a German hotel
summary: German broadcaster WDR reports that 15 hotel guests at the Phantasialand resort were exposed to chlorine gas after a technical defect, which the widely shared headline ties to a Microsoft 365 outage.

title: Australian supermarket Coles hit by a cybersecurity incident
summary: Coles, one of Australia's largest supermarket chains, has posted an update confirming a cybersecurity incident.

title: AI coding assistants decoded a 1994 Jeep's engine computer
summary: A video shows Claude Code and Codex working out how a 1994 Jeep's engine control unit works, using a $3 Arduino board as the connection.

title: A cross-site scripting flaw in uBlock Origin
summary: A security write-up describes a 'universal XSS' bug in uBlock Origin, the popular ad blocker, triggered through its element picker — the tool you use to click on and hide parts of a page.

title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
summary: Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard, which ranks speech-recognition models (software that turns spoken audio into text), now includes Egyptian English and Nigerian English test sets.

title: Hugging Face and OpenRouter team up to make open AI models easy to use
summary: Hugging Face, where nearly every major open-weight AI model is published, is partnering with OpenRouter, a service that runs those models at scale and routes each request across more than 80 providers based on live measurements of how each one is performing.

title: Report: Windows 11 tracks which AI coding tools you use
summary: A developer's blog post, widely discussed on Hacker News, says Windows 11 collects data on which coding agents and developer tools are installed and used on a machine.

title: Optimizely breach served malware on major sites, including Zoom and GitLab
summary: Report URI says Optimizely — a widely used tool companies add to their websites to test different page designs — was compromised and used to deliver malware through brands such as Zoom and GitLab.

title: Carnegie Mellon puts computer science courses on YouTube for free
summary: Carnegie Mellon University, one of the top computer science schools in the US, is publishing its computer science courses on YouTube at no cost.

title: Anthropic maps out possible futures for an AI economy
summary: Anthropic published 'Scenarios for our economic future', starting from an honest premise: nobody yet knows whether AI will bring unprecedented growth, widespread unemployment, neither, or something else.

title: GitHub rebuilds Git storage so thousands of AI agents can work in one project
summary: GitHub described a new architecture for storing Git repositories, built so that thousands of AI agents can push changes to a single repository at the same time.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic upgraded its two most capable models, Claude Fable 5.

title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
summary: OpenAI announced two new models, GPT-6.

title: Google's AI answers are cutting search traffic by 40%, report says
summary: A new analysis says Google's AI-generated answers are reducing the traffic websites get from search by 40%, because people get their answer without clicking through.

title: GitHub and Microsoft turn AI bug reports into actual fixes
summary: In a pilot called Codename MDASH, GitHub and Microsoft filtered thousands of raw AI-found bugs down to 99 checked, private reports — each with a suggested fix — for six widely used open-source projects.

title: 'Java4Shell': a serious security flaw in Java
summary: Researchers disclosed a flaw in OpenJDK, the standard version of Java, that can let attackers run their own code when a system processes Base64 data — an extremely common way of encoding information.

title: GitHub's Agent Host Protocol lets AI sessions follow you between devices
summary: GitHub built the Agent Host Protocol, an open standard that keeps an AI agent's working session available across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.

title: Harvard study: AI coding agents moved the bottleneck to code review
summary: Harvard researchers found that AI coding agents shifted where software work gets stuck: writing code is faster, but reviewing that code has become the slow step.

title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Neon, the newest model in its Gemini AI family, a week after it announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

title: AI agents asked better questions than KPMG accountants in an audit trial
summary: European Business Magazine reports on an audit trial in which AI agents asked better questions than KPMG's human accountants.

title: Microsoft unveils seven new AI models at Ignite
summary: At its Ignite 2026 conference, Microsoft announced seven new AI models, pitched on 'scalable price-performance': a range of sizes, so businesses can pay less for simpler tasks.

title: Serious security flaws found in Nginx, a common web server
summary: Security firm Wiz reports flaws in Nginx, the software that serves a large share of the world's websites, that could let attackers run their own code without logging in.

title: How AI helps turn field notes into Ebola situation reports
summary: Anthropic published a feature on the Ebola response in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, where health workers text their daily counts of fevers, recoveries, and deaths over WhatsApp.

title: DaisyRose-27B: a strong agent model trained on a small budget
summary: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, its first model, built on Qwen3.

title: Running a 180-billion-parameter model on 32GB of RAM
summary: Hugging Face shows how to run a 180-billion-parameter 'mixture of experts' model, one that switches on only a few specialist sub-networks for each word, on a machine with just 32GB of memory.

title: Claude solves two open problems in black hole physics
summary: Anthropic reports that Claude, its AI model, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes — questions researchers had not yet answered.

title: Critical security flaw found in OpenSSL
summary: OpenSSL, the software that encrypts traffic for a huge share of websites and apps, has a buffer overflow bug rated 9.

title: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data leaked
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that hackers leaked customer data from Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan.

title: UK admits it secretly ordered Apple to weaken encryption
summary: The UK government has been forced to admit it issued Apple a secret order about encryption — the technology that keeps your messages and files private.

title: GitHub launches open-source projects for accessibility
summary: GitHub introduced Replica and the Open Source Accessibility Framework, two new open-source projects aimed at collaboration and inclusion.

title: Why AI fine-tuning jobs run longer than expected
summary: A Hugging Face blog post analyses 272 real production runs to predict how long fine-tuning — retraining an AI model on your own data — actually takes on shared GPU clusters.

title: PostgreSQL 19 is out
summary: PostgreSQL 19, a new major version of one of the most widely used open-source databases, has been released.

title: A claimed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis has mathematicians buzzing
summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge has posted a claimed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a question about prime numbers that has stood unsolved for over a century, and leading mathematicians including Terence Tao are already writing about it.

title: Inkling 2 Mini: a capable AI model built to run on your own computer
summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open model that can work with text and images and is designed for local use.

title: Signal pushes back on AI agents reading your phone screen
summary: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, published a post on restricting AI agents built into mobile operating systems from capturing your data.

title: Backblaze's privacy policy now says it can sell data for advertising
summary: Backblaze, a popular cloud backup service, now explicitly states in its privacy policy that it sells data for advertising purposes, according to a widely discussed Hacker News thread.

title: Research paper: AI chatbots may carry hidden commercial incentives
summary: A new paper calls it "The Hungry Butler Effect": concealed commercial incentives in large language models that can erode how rigorous their answers are.

title: Valkey swaps the skiplist for a B+ tree and cuts memory use
summary: Valkey, the open-source in-memory database that forked from Redis, replaced the skiplist behind its sorted sets with a B+ tree.

title: Harness adapters: tuning a model for the agent tool you actually use
summary: Hugging Face introduced harness adapters, a way to train an AI model with reinforcement learning on your own set of tasks inside your chosen agent harness — the software that wraps a model with tools and instructions.

title: The Riemann Hypothesis proof gets a computer-checked verification
summary: Previously covered on 2026-11-21: mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a claimed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a century-old question about prime numbers.

title: Two AI providers disclose incidents with customer prompts
summary: OpenRouter, a service that routes AI requests to many model providers, published a post on data processing incidents at those providers, and Together.

title: A pill for pancreatic cancer is called the biggest breakthrough in decades
summary: The Guardian reports that daraxonrasib, a pill to treat pancreatic cancer, is being hailed as the biggest advance against the disease in decades.

title: Git fixes six security flaws — update your tools
summary: Git, the version-control system behind almost all software projects, released updates for six security vulnerabilities.

title: Pandex gives AI agents direct access to official European law
summary: Pandex is a new service that lets AI agents look up official European legal texts through MCP, a standard way of connecting AI tools to outside data.

title: LLMs can read and write programs straight from a hex dump
summary: A blog post shows large language models reading and writing executable files byte by byte from a hex dump — the raw numbers a computer actually runs — without any source code or programming language in between.

title: Inkling 2 Mini squeezed into 5.4 GB of memory
summary: Previously covered on 2026-11-21: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open model built to run locally.
